quote_steps: An engineer reviews your drawing, sample or concept.
Your quote comes with DFM and material selection.
Prototype parts, then a production tool designed, built and trialled.

faqs_moulding.q: What materials can Ertone injection mould?
faqs_moulding.a: Mainly polycarbonate (PC), polypropylene (PP), polystyrene (GPPS), ABS and nylon (PA), including high quality clear parts. Tell us how the part will be used and we will recommend the right polymer.

faqs_moulding.q: How long does it take to produce a new mould tool?
faqs_moulding.a: It depends on the size and complexity of the part and the tool. Your quote sets out the tooling lead time, and if you already have a tool we can move it to Ertone instead.

faqs_moulding.q: What size components can you produce?
faqs_moulding.a: Parts from 1 gram up to 4 kilograms, on presses from 100 to 600 tonnes. That covers small precision components through to large structural mouldings.

faqs_moulding.q: What does the Ertone injection moulding service include?
faqs_moulding.a: Design and material advice, tool making or tool transfer, sampling and trials, volume production, then printing, welding, assembly, packing and delivery. One team looks after your part from drawing to dispatch.
